title: Send Telegram Alerts When a Web Page Changes in Python
description: Monitor any allowed vendor or status page and push instant notifications to your phone when content updates. Learn how ten lines of Python leverage checksums and Telegram bots to automate change tracking.
code:
import hashlib, requests
url = "https://example.com/status"
cur = hashlib.sha1(
    requests.get(url).content).hexdigest()
if cur != "old_hash_value":
    api = "https://api.telegram.org/botX/"
    data = {"chat_id": 123, "text": url}
    requests.post(api + "sendMessage",
                  json=data)
    print("Telegram alert delivered")

beats.voice: There is a 10-line Python pattern that alerts your phone the second a vendor page changes.
Fetch the live content and calculate a fast SHA1 hash to fingerprint the current page state.
If that fingerprint differs from your stored checksum, hit Telegram's bot API with a single POST.
Run it on a periodic timer, and you receive an immediate alert the moment changes publish.

kit_readme:
SETUP
1. Ensure Python 3.8+ is installed.
2. Install required package:
   pip install requests
3. Create a Telegram bot via @BotFather to get your TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN.
4. Retrieve your chat ID (e.g., via @userinfobot).

HOW IT WORKS
tool.py requests the target web page, hashes the raw content using SHA-256, and compares it against a cached hash stored in monitor_cache.json.
If the hash changes, it posts a formatted message directly to your Telegram chat and updates the cache.

Usage:
python tool.py --url "https://example.com/status" --token "YOUR_BOT_TOKEN" --chat-id "YOUR_CHAT_ID"

Test safely with dry-run mode:
python tool.py --url "https://example.com/status" --dry-run

ADAPTING IT
- Schedule with cron (Linux/macOS) or Task Scheduler (Windows) to run every 15 minutes.
- Environment variables: set TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID in your environment to avoid passing them via flags.
- For sites with dynamic scripts or ads, strip non-content tags using BeautifulSoup before hashing.

LIMITATIONS
Pages featuring rotating ads, CSRF tokens, dynamic timestamps, or client-side JavaScript rendering (SPA) will trigger false alarms unless filtered first. Only monitor pages whose terms of service permit automated retrieval.
